column2: On the authority of ʿAbdullāh ibn Busr, who said: “A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah,
the laws of Islam have become too many for us, so [tell us of] a comprehensive door to which we can hold fast.

He said: Let your tongue remain moist with the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.” Recorded by Imam Aḥmad with this wording, and by al-Tirmidhī, Ibn Mājah and Ibn Ḥibbān in his Ṣaḥīḥ with this meaning; al-Tirmidhī said: “Ḥasan gharīb.”
This man's question to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is one of many examples of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asking about the matters of the religion,
and all of that shows their virtue, their nobility, their being foremost in every good and their eagerness for every good. What is meant by the laws that had become many is the voluntary deeds.

This Companion wanted to know one of the paths of good that he could give special attention to in order to gain the reward of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. As for the obligations, all of them are required,
and the Muslim must hold fast to them all. The Prophet ﷺ answered by telling him to persevere in the remembrance of Allah and to keep his tongue moist with His remembrance.

Remembrance (dhikr) is of two kinds, general and specific. General remembrance includes the prayers, reciting the Qurʾān, learning and teaching knowledge, praising Allah, extolling Him, and declaring Him free and holy above everything that does not befit Him.

Specific remembrance is praising and extolling Allah, glorifying Him (tasbīḥ), declaring His oneness (tahlīl), magnifying Him (takbīr) and praising Him (taḥmīd); it is what is paired with supplication, so one says:

“remembrance and supplication”, or “supplications and words of remembrance”. This deed is easy for a person and of great reward with Allah. It is established in the two Ṣaḥīḥs—and it is the last hadith in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī—that he ﷺ said:

“Two phrases are beloved to the Most Merciful, light on the tongue and heavy in the Balance: Subḥān Allāh wa-bi-ḥamdih (Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him), Subḥān Allāh al-ʿAẓīm (Glory be to Allah the Magnificent).”
The Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) were eager to ask about the matters of their religion.
The hadith shows the merit of the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and of persevering in it.
